# Task context

A Python program has been ported to Node.js. You are VERIFYING the port.

- Python source:      /workspace/dataset/boltons/test6.py
- Python reference:   /workspace/dataset/test6_executable   (pre-compiled, Python 3.12, run it directly; NEVER use the 'python' command)
- Node port:          /output/test6.mjs  plus libraries under /output/lib/**/*.mjs

The program takes three REQUIRED string options --a --b --c, builds a
boltons OrderedMultiDict, and prints 6 lines (repr of the OMD three times,
then getlist / keys / items results).

## Differential harness (USE THIS)

    /tmp/dt.sh [ARGS...]

It runs the reference executable and the Node port with identical argv and
byte-compares stdout, stderr AND exit status. It prints exactly "PASS" on a
match, or a "FAIL" report with hex dumps and diffs. Exit 0 = match.

IMPORTANT: the harness invokes the port through the shim
/tmp/prog/test6_executable so that argparse derives an IDENTICAL program name
on both sides. Therefore NO output normalisation happens and the comparison is
raw bytes. Do NOT compare by running "node /output/test6.mjs" yourself --
argparse legitimately derives the prog name from basename(argv[0]), so the
usage/error text and even the line wrapping would differ for reasons that are
NOT bugs. Always go through /tmp/dt.sh.

## Rules

- READ-ONLY on /output and /workspace. Do NOT edit, create or delete any file
  there. Use /tmp for scratch files.
- A NUL byte cannot be passed through argv; do not report that as a bug.
- Be efficient: batch many characters into a single argv string (e.g. 200-500
  code points per argument) so one invocation covers many cases, then binary
  search to isolate any failure to a specific character.
- Every mismatch you report MUST come with an exact, self-contained shell
  command that reproduces it via /tmp/dt.sh.


# Your dimension: omd-semantics

Differentially fuzz the OrderedMultiDict semantics and the printed data structure.
Cover: --b equal to --c; --b different from --c; all three arguments identical; empty-string key
with non-empty values and vice versa; keys/values that are digits, floats, booleans-as-text
("True", "None"), whitespace-only, very long (10k+ chars), containing newlines/tabs/carriage
returns/backslashes/quotes in every combination (single quote only, double quote only, both,
backslash before a quote, trailing backslash); strings that are valid Python repr syntax
themselves; multi-line values. Verify all six printed lines byte-for-byte, especially the
quote-selection rule and that items() shows only the LAST value for the repeated key while the
OMD repr shows BOTH pairs. Also check that the number of output lines and trailing newline are
exact.

Report every mismatch you found and could reproduce. If you found none, return an empty mismatches array and describe your coverage honestly. Do not invent mismatches.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: run the Python reference executable and the Node
# port with identical argv, then byte-compare stdout, stderr and exit status.
#
# /tmp/prog/test6_executable is a shim whose basename matches the reference
# executable, so argparse derives the same prog name on both sides and NO
# output normalisation is needed -- the comparison is raw bytes.
#
# Usage:  /tmp/dt.sh [ARGS...]
# Output: "PASS", or a "FAIL" report. Exit 0 on match, 1 otherwise.

PY=/workspace/dataset/test6_executable
SHIM=/tmp/prog/test6_executable

if [ ! -f "$SHIM" ]; then
  mkdir -p /tmp/prog
  printf "import('/output/test6.mjs');\n" > "$SHIM"
fi

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

"$PY" "$@" >"$tmp/py.out" 2>"$tmp/py.err"
py_code=$?
node "$SHIM" "$@" >"$tmp/js.out" 2>"$tmp/js.err"
js_code=$?

ok=1
[ "$py_code" != "$js_code" ] && ok=0
cmp -s "$tmp/py.out" "$tmp/js.out" || ok=0
cmp -s "$tmp/py.err" "$tmp/js.err" || ok=0

if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then
  echo "PASS"
  exit 0
fi

echo "FAIL  argv:"
for a in "$@"; do printf '  arg=[%s] hex=[%s]\n' "$a" "$(printf '%s' "$a" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"; done
echo "exit: py=$py_code js=$js_code"
echo "--- stdout diff (py vs js) ---"
diff <(od -c "$tmp/py.out") <(od -c "$tmp/js.out") | head -40
echo "--- stderr diff (py vs js) ---"
diff <(od -c "$tmp/py.err") <(od -c "$tmp/js.err") | head -40
exit 1
---

#!/bin/bash
# Sweep code points [START,END] in chunks of CH per argument, 3 args per invocation.
START=$1; END=$2; CH=${3:-4000}
mkfmt(){ # $1=from $2=to -> prints the string
  local f="" i
  for ((i=$1;i<=$2;i++)); do
    if (( i>=0xD800 && i<=0xDFFF )); then continue; fi
    printf -v tmp '\\U%08x' $i
    f+=$tmp
  done
  printf "$f"
}
cp_=$START
fail=0; n=0
while (( cp_ <= END )); do
  a_end=$((cp_+CH-1)); (( a_end>END )) && a_end=$END
  A=$(mkfmt $cp_ $a_end); cp_=$((a_end+1))
  B=""; C=""
  if (( cp_ <= END )); then b_end=$((cp_+CH-1)); (( b_end>END )) && b_end=$END; B=$(mkfmt $cp_ $b_end); cp_=$((b_end+1)); fi
  if (( cp_ <= END )); then c_end=$((cp_+CH-1)); (( c_end>END )) && c_end=$END; C=$(mkfmt $cp_ $c_end); cp_=$((c_end+1)); fi
  n=$((n+1))
  out=$(/tmp/dt.sh --a "$A" --b "$B" --c "$C" 2>&1)
  if [ "$out" != "PASS" ]; then
    fail=$((fail+1))
    echo "=== FAIL chunk ending cp=$((cp_-1)) (A started $((cp_ - 3*CH))) ==="
    echo "$out" | head -12
  fi
done
echo "SWEEP $START..$END TOTAL=$n FAILED=$fail"
SCRIPT

#!/bin/bash
# Proper code-point sweep. Generation happens in a UTF-8 locale so that bash's
# printf actually emits UTF-8 bytes; the comparison itself runs with the
# original (locale-unset) environment via `env -u`.
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
START=$1; END=$2; CH=${3:-3000}

mkstr(){ # $1=from $2=to
  local f="" i t
  for ((i=$1;i<=$2;i++)); do
    if (( i>=0xD800 && i<=0xDFFF )); then continue; fi
    printf -v t '\\U%08x' $i
    f+=$t
  done
  printf "$f"
}

cp_=$START; fail=0; n=0
while (( cp_ <= END )); do
  s=$cp_
  a1=$cp_; a2=$((cp_+CH-1)); (( a2>END )) && a2=$END; A=$(mkstr $a1 $a2); cp_=$((a2+1))
  B=""; C=""; b1=0; b2=0; c1=0; c2=0
  if (( cp_ <= END )); then b1=$cp_; b2=$((cp_+CH-1)); (( b2>END )) && b2=$END; B=$(mkstr $b1 $b2); cp_=$((b2+1)); fi
  if (( cp_ <= END )); then c1=$cp_; c2=$((cp_+CH-1)); (( c2>END )) && c2=$END; C=$(mkstr $c1 $c2); cp_=$((c2+1)); fi
  # sanity: generation must not have left literal backslash escapes behind
  case "$A" in *'\U'*|*'\u'*) echo "GENFAIL at $a1..$a2"; exit 2;; esac
  n=$((n+1))
  out=$(env -u LC_ALL -u LC_CTYPE /tmp/dt.sh --a "$A" --b "$B" --c "$C" 2>&1)
  if [ "$out" != "PASS" ]; then
    fail=$((fail+1))
    echo "=== FAIL chunk A=$a1..$a2 B=$b1..$b2 C=$c1..$c2 ==="
    echo "$out" | head -14
  fi
done
echo "SWEEP $START..$END TOTAL=$n FAILED=$fail"

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Bisect a code point range down to individual offending code points.
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
mkstr(){ local f="" i t; for ((i=$1;i<=$2;i++)); do (( i>=0xD800 && i<=0xDFFF )) && continue; printf -v t '\\U%08x' $i; f+=$t; done; printf "$f"; }
tst(){ local A; A=$(mkstr $1 $2); out=$(env -u LC_ALL -u LC_CTYPE /tmp/dt.sh --a "$A" --b b --c c 2>&1); [ "$out" == "PASS" ]; }
scan(){ # linear scan, report each bad cp
  local i
  for ((i=$1;i<=$2;i++)); do
    (( i>=0xD800 && i<=0xDFFF )) && continue
    if ! tst $i $i; then printf 'BAD cp=%d (U+%04X)\n' $i $i; fi
  done
}
bisect(){ # $1 lo $2 hi : recursive halving to find ranges containing failures
  local lo=$1 hi=$2 mid
  if tst $lo $hi; then return; fi
  if (( hi-lo < 40 )); then scan $lo $hi; return; fi
  mid=$(( (lo+hi)/2 ))
  bisect $lo $mid
  bisect $((mid+1)) $hi
}
bisect $1 $2
echo "BISECT DONE $1..$2"
